reading.body:
Equinix SV5 is a 93,495 square foot retail colocation facility in San Jose that publishes no megawatt figure for its power capacity. The operator specifies N+1 power redundancy and N+2 cooling redundancy with a minimum cabinet density of 5 kVA, which qualifies it to host enterprise and network service workloads requiring high availability. Without a published power figure, its absolute scale relative to AI training infrastructure cannot be assessed from available data.

SV5 is one of 12 facilities in Equinix's Silicon Valley campus, which the operator describes as the region's largest retail colocation footprint. Within California, 103 mapped data center facilities exist, but only 11 publish megawatt figures, totaling 365 MW of publicly disclosed capacity. SV5 does not rank among those 11 disclosed facilities; it ranks 12th in the state by published megawatt capacity only because it publishes no capacity at all.

The facility serves a retail colocation customer base rather than being purpose-built for AI training. Equinix's Silicon Valley campus across its six named sites hosts over 10,500 customers including 4,900 enterprises and 2,000 network service providers, suggesting a general-purpose workload mix rather than the compute density required for large-scale AI training. Whether SV5 matters to AI scaling depends on whether its customer base includes AI training tenants and what power density those tenants operate at, neither of which is published.
